name: Orbit 0.4.8
body:
## 0.4.8 — 2026-11-13

Orbit 0.4.8 adds reviewed HubSpot imports from a connected account, keeps completed-meeting follow-up visible until its goal is met or someone stops it, and adds on-demand deal-risk task filing. Orbit still runs on rer 0.2.107.

- **Review a connected HubSpot import before applying it.** Connect a HubSpot private app with read access, inspect the source inventory, and pull companies, contacts, deals, notes, calls, meetings and tasks into the existing mapping and review flow. Pulls retain their progress and can resume after a rate limit or interruption. Imported rows keep their source links; applying and undoing use Orbit's existing review rules. Orbit writes nothing back to HubSpot. Pulls are limited to 1,000 objects of each type. Leads, email activity, attachments and workflows are excluded; unsupported properties need separate reconciliation. Imported meetings are timeline history, not completed-meeting signals. Credentials and staged provider pages stay out of archives; reconnect and pull again after a restore. Explicit contact erasure withdraws staged HubSpot data, while ordinary import undo and duplicate reconciliation do not.
- **A completed meeting can leave a lasting follow-up.** Review its goal, stop condition, owner and due time before accepting. The deal shows the accepted follow-up and its linked work. A reply records evidence without treating the goal as complete; reaching the recorded stage or a person's explicit stop closes the obligation and cancels its remaining linked work. Written stop conditions remain for people to interpret; Orbit closes automatically only at the exact selected goal stage. Drafts still need separate review and approval before sending. Restored follow-ups retain their history but stay paused with linked reminders until fresh acceptance and any required approval.
- **Start a deal-risk agent when you choose.** From one deal, file its current cited findings as tasks assigned to you under company policy. The run shows what was filed, already present, waiting for review or refused. Running it again preserves an existing task, including one you completed or cancelled. Recorded due times carry into proposed tasks. This is an on-demand run for that deal, not scheduled monitoring.
- **Agents can use the configured opportunity AI assistance.** An agent can inspect the native input and request an unsent draft or a recommendation explanation under company policy. The request binds the exact input, provider and model; changed records require a fresh preview. Results cite the supplied evidence, and saved drafts grant no permission to send. This does not add general agent coverage or automatic outreach.
- **Mailchimp handoffs check the audience more carefully.** Choosing an audience registers Orbit's webhook, and handoffs wait for Mailchimp to check its public HTTPS address. Before a handoff, Orbit reconciles changed member states, retains stops across contact merges and address changes, and tracks earlier linked member identities. Scheduled processing now advances pending permanent-deletion requests; refusal and uncertain outcomes remain visible. After reconnection or archive restore, held deletion requests need the owner's confirmation. Orbit still requires recorded marketing consent and sends no campaigns.
- **Captured evidence does not grant contact permission.** A contact created from an unlinked event starts as Do not contact. Recreating a previously erased address also starts stopped and requires explicit permission before outreach.
- **Shared records and draft reviews are easier to read.** Shared records show permitted names, currency amounts, dates and custom-field labels with suitable editing controls. Draft review names missing merge fields in ordinary language.
- **Setup and archive controls explain the next step.** Capture, AI, Slack, Mailchimp and calling settings include setup guidance. Archive transfers show their start and size, with copyable support details. Older native archive generations remain recognized. An installation without its public origin configured can answer health checks without failing while constructing the agent door.

Account proposals remain limited to selected written evidence and the existing three proposal types. Scheduled graph maintenance, transcripts, licensed enrichment and broader stakeholder inference remain incomplete. Workflow undo remains partial. The earlier erasure limitations remain: a former sponsor or approver can still appear by name in a colleague's timeline and audit rows, and an approver's name stays in the search index until it is rebuilt. These changes do not establish complete agent coverage or live-provider acceptance.

Update from 0.4.7 in place after stopping writes and taking a private backup. Apply the three pending migrations once, in order, before the new Worker serves: they add follow-up obligations and linked work, add private HubSpot import staging, then remove the broad contact-delete trigger so staging is withdrawn only for explicit privacy erasure. Preserve the migration ledger and all already-applied migration files; do not replay the graph-proposal migration from 0.4.7. No new provider setting is required to retain existing features. To use connected HubSpot imports, supply its read-only private-app access in Imports. Existing Mailchimp connections should be checked again to register and validate the webhook.

name: Orbit 0.4.7
body:
## 0.4.7 — 2026-11-12

Orbit 0.4.7 adds cited account-correction proposals for review, makes agent draft content consistent with native drafts, and explains Slack setup and agent capabilities more clearly. Orbit still runs on rer 0.2.107.

- **Review cited account corrections one at a time.** With fresh consent for selected company, contact, deal and captured-mail evidence, an agent can propose a contact's job title, a deal's close date and a question about the missing decision-maker. Each appears in native review with its source quote and who proposed it. Accept, edit or decline each separately; accepting the question acknowledges it without creating a contact or assigning a stakeholder role. Proposing changes never applies them automatically or changes contactability. Disconnecting or replacing the evidence source withdraws its pending proposals; reconnecting does not revive them. A changed field makes related drafts stale.
- **Agent drafts use the same whitespace handling as native drafts.** Creating or editing a manual draft through the agent door now trims the subject and body, refuses content that is only whitespace, and shows the normalized content in review. The existing limits of each interface still apply. Saving a draft grants no approval to send it.
- **Slack setup explains what it needs before you connect.** Settings lists required and optional permissions, callback addresses, event subscriptions, permitted notice fields, how credentials are held, and the risk that channel membership can change. This information remains visible after disconnection. Credentials stay out of archives; reconnecting requires confirming channels and mappings and does not replay old notices or actions.
- **Workflow previews and history explain their effects.** Previews separate internal changes from external webhooks. Execution history shows linked record names, when events occurred and when versions were activated. An activity logged after activation but occurring before it records a skipped outcome without running actions; activities already recorded before activation are not replayed.
- **The agent guide matches discovery more closely.** Installation facts, person-only screens, device behavior and reviewed import doors have explicit explanations in discovery and the guide. These descriptions add no new actions and do not claim complete agent coverage.

Account proposals remain limited to selected written evidence and these three proposal types. Scheduled graph maintenance, transcripts, licensed enrichment and broader stakeholder inference remain incomplete. Workflow undo remains partial. The earlier erasure limitations remain: a former sponsor or approver can still appear by name in a colleague's timeline and audit rows, and an approver's name stays in the search index until it is rebuilt.

Update from 0.4.6 in place after taking a private backup. One migration preserves the existing capture-proposal rows while adding question proposals and withdrawal handling. It refuses unexpected customizations of that table for review; resolve those before updating. Older native archive generations remain recognized. No new provider setting is required.

name: Orbit 0.4.6
body:
Orbit 0.4.6 erases more of what your agents recorded when you erase a person or a contact, explains a missing mail sender before you approve a draft, stops notifying you about your own actions, and carries the fixes found by people trying Orbit for the first time. Orbit still runs on rer 0.2.107.

- **Erasing a person or a contact also erases what your agents recorded about them.** Erasing a person now removes their name from what agents recorded as their sponsor and from the approver marks on agent actions that person approved. Erasing a contact now removes the values an agent saved about that contact in approvals, call outcomes, the audit trail and events. If an agent retries a call for a contact you have erased, Orbit answers that the contact was erased instead of creating it again. An agent following the change feed keeps working across a contact erasure and carries on from where it was. Not covered yet: a former sponsor or approver of a colleague's agent action can still appear by name in that colleague's timeline and audit rows, and an approver's name stays in the search index until the index is rebuilt.
- **The Mail page explains a missing sender before you approve a draft.** If no mail sender is set up, a draft now says so where you would approve or schedule it, with a link to set one up, and your draft stays saved. Settings › Customer mail sender lists each missing setting by name with what to do about it, instead of a count.
- **You are no longer notified of your own actions.** Something you do yourself, such as sending a message, no longer lands in your own notifications. Other people, agents, providers and scheduled sends still notify as before.
- **HubSpot notes import, and early selections are kept.** A HubSpot notes export with its normal column labels (Record ID, Note Body, Activity date, Activity assigned to and the associated record columns) now maps without renaming anything, and the moving guide lists those labels. Files and a source you choose before the page has finished loading are no longer lost.
- **Integrations explains API access and groups connections truthfully.** Settings › Integrations has an API access section that explains how to let a reporting tool read selected deals and fields, and opens the guide on your own installation with steps you can run from your browser's console. Connections are grouped as Connected to Orbit, Not connected, and Connection status unavailable, with clearer wording for products that need attention or are waiting for a first booking.
- **A saved form keeps its compile step after you reload.** Open a saved form after a reload and its wording comes back into the editor with the compile and approve steps available.
- **Dates read in your locale.** Dates and times follow your browser's locale (month first for workspaces in the Americas time zones), and typed dates such as Expected close and Schedule for later are text fields that show the order they expect. A date that is impossible, or not in that order, is refused with that hint rather than guessed.
- **The queue names what caused it.** A deal that moves to Now because of new evidence names the event that caused it rather than saying its priority rose, and the deal timeline and Today list no longer repeat the same label twice.

It updates 0.4.5 in place and keeps every row. It adds two migrations, so take a private backup first: one adds a rule that keeps a person's own direct actions out of their notifications, and one replaces three internal rules so that rule does not disturb agent access. Nothing in your existing data is rewritten.

name: Orbit 0.4.5
body:
Orbit 0.4.5 keeps a stopped or detached Business from pulling decisions, takes an erased person off your Business team list, and carries the changes made since 0.4.4. Orbit now runs on rer 0.2.107.

- **A stopped or detached Business can no longer pull decisions.** A Business-linked Orbit now answers a Business pull only while that Business is positively running; if the Business is stopped or detached, the pull is refused. An older approval that came from a Business that has since stopped is refused too, including an approval saved before approvals recorded which Business they belong to. When you pair Orbit with a new Business, an approval from the old one stays with the old one.
- **Erasing a person also removes them from your Business team list.** Erasing a person now takes them off the team list the Business signs and keeps them off it, so a later Business update that still names them does not bring them back. People erased on earlier versions drop off at your next Business update. Orbit keeps only a value-free marker of each erased person for this, never a name, address or id. An archive restore does not carry that list of erased people: a Business that re-pairs after a restore and still lists an erased person could invite them again.
- **Erasing one person no longer touches another person's agent records.** Where two people's email addresses end alike, such as al@ and sal@, erasing one no longer selects the other's agent records. Erasing a person does not yet remove the names agents recorded about them; that work is still to come.
- **Updating `rer`.** The pinned `rer` is now 0.2.107. Its `rer deploy --dry-run` finishes cleanly, setup-token retirement tolerates a partial Cloudflare list, and `rer signin` prints the link for a custom domain. Update the checkout with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

It updates 0.4.4 in place and keeps every row. It adds three migrations, so take a private backup first: one new table for retired agent-door references, one that removes only the Business pull records provably copied across two different Businesses (every audit record stays), and one new table for the erased-people list. Nothing else in your data is changed.

name: Orbit 0.4.4
body:
Orbit 0.4.4 keeps a truthful record of what each form visitor was shown, gives Reports one list of pages, and carries the changes made since 0.4.3. Orbit now runs on rer 0.2.96.

- **Forms keep a truthful record of what the visitor was shown.** Each submission now keeps the wording, the form's revision and the time. A form with consent wording records that wording and whether the box was ticked. A form without it shows one line saying that sending the enquiry asks for a one-to-one follow-up and does not subscribe the visitor to marketing, and records that line. Settings › Forms shows the record beside the submission. A new contact is marked contactable only when the visitor accepted what the page showed; a contact you had already stopped stays stopped, and sending the same submission again keeps its original record and time. A form published before this update that did not show the follow-up line records no basis, and its new contacts are marked do not contact until you approve and publish the form again. A submission's name, email and company land on the right contact and company, a deal opens in the pipeline and stage you chose, and a deal made by a form names that form.
- **Reports is one list, and each report has its own page.** Reports lists your dashboards first, with your default marked, then your reports: the forecast (in a USD workspace, for a full operator), your saved reports and the built-in reports. New creates a dashboard or a custom report. Each report has its own address, computes when you open it, and recomputes in place when you change the period. The records behind a figure open in the same side panel a dashboard uses, and Report options (saved results, sharing, versions, edit) and the forecast's inputs and history sit there too. You no longer type a report key or a version. A reviewed custom-report preview saves after you change its period, and saving a result keeps Report options open.
- **Closed deals read as closed.** A won or lost deal's header shows its outcome with the date, such as "Won 4 Nov 2026", then the reason, with no Why NOW badge or next action. Records marks won and lost deals, and the board keeps them in their own Won and Lost columns.
- **Undoing a workflow can archive the deals it created.** When you undo a workflow run or version, a deal that workflow created is closed as lost, with a reason naming the undone version, only if nobody has edited it or added a contact, activity, task, message or signal since. Otherwise it is left as it is and listed with who touched it last and when. Undo sends nothing and cancels no scheduled message. Workflow undo is still partly done: the contract keeps it partial, and choosing which owner rules to undo is not complete.
- **Team access.** The Analyst role reads NOW, Records (list and board), deals, contacts, companies, the Brief and Shared records, with no editing controls and with writes still refused. An invited person's local sign-in link opens a styled "Sign in to Orbit" page that lists them to choose. A collaborator's settings name only the owners of the deals they can read. A shared record someone cannot open shows "Record is unavailable", and the message now stays when the list finishes loading after it. Equal access for every operator across every workspace action is not claimed: the contract keeps Equal operators partial.
- **API credentials and agents.** A new guide, Create and use an API credential, gives copyable browser-console steps, and a refused credential request now names the missing or invalid keys. An API credential, active or revoked, cannot approve an exact saved message: the request is refused and no draft, message or mail submission follows. The agent door's guide lists its current tools and resources. The installation owner's agent can save a draft of an existing workflow without activating it, preview and then delete one saved report (the company's policy decides whether it runs or waits for a named person), and read then rotate the private Capture address. The door can also answer a signed pull from Business with its decisions, carrying no arguments, names or record contents, and ends everything it derived from Business when Business stops. The contract keeps each of these agent-door and API-credential clauses partial.
- **Opt-out after an upgrade.** An installation that already had users keeps one-to-one opt-out on, with the retained basis shown in Settings at desktop and phone widths and after a reload. A message approved before the setting existed keeps its original bytes and unsubscribe group, and nothing is submitted to the provider again. Opt-out choices for connected mailboxes, sequences, batches and workflows are not covered by this and stay partial. A signed unsubscribe refuses a new draft to that contact, and refuses the earlier draft's approval at any hour.
- **A complete archive.** Export and restore carry every current category of Orbit data, including captured evidence and Slack routing, notices and deletion history, without secrets or authority. A Slack deletion still pending when a contact was erased restores as held, and nothing is sent until an administrator reconnects and confirms.
- **Smaller fixes.** A next action proposed beside a booked meeting or reply can be accepted after you accept its link, and a stale review still refuses. Notes brought in by an import show the import as their source. A deal-risk citation of an overdue task opens that task, and a citation of a sent message opens its receipt. A connected provider that answers with a redirect stops intake with a plain message. The Sender setup page shows the right hosted commands: a new sender address needs a full deploy. The website recipe's Node example is prepared from the values you fill into the published form. The homepage leads with Orbit as a product.

It updates 0.4.3 in place and keeps every row. It adds one migration, which adds the agent door's replay and decision-feed records and a retention date on its saved calls; nothing else in your data is changed.

name: Orbit 0.4.3
body:
Orbit 0.4.3 starts first-run setup from what the platform already knows, and carries the changes made since 0.4.2.

- **First-run setup starts filled in.** The first-run form now starts with the Business name, your name and the time zone the platform already knows, so you confirm them instead of typing them again. A value the platform has not set reads as before.
- **A dashboard can be removed.** In Edit tiles, the dashboard's owner or the installation owner can remove a dashboard after one confirmation. Its versions, sharing, schedule and everyone's default go with it, and Slack notices still waiting to send for it are held. The saved reports and forecast views behind its tiles stay.
- **Report periods read as dates.** A report's Period, in previews and saved history, shows dates and times in the workspace's time zone instead of raw timestamps. The open-opportunities report, which has no period, says when it was read.
- **The current month follows the workspace's time zone.** A new forecast or dashboard starts on the current month in the workspace's time zone, not in UTC, so it no longer opens on the wrong month at the turn of a month. Calendar capture windows use the same dates in every browser time zone.
- **Disconnecting Mailchimp asks first.** Disconnect Mailchimp now explains that it deletes the saved key and the webhook address, and that Mailchimp's unsubscribes stop reaching Orbit until you connect again, then waits for you to confirm.
- **Clearer focus, readable small text, bigger phone targets.** A focused text field, menu or text box shows focus on its own border instead of a second ring around it. Text that was smaller than 13 px is now 13 px. At phone width, every button, link and expandable row you tap is at least 44 px tall.
- **A white content area.** The main content area under the header is now plain white; the header keeps its paper tone.
- **Behind the scenes.** The contract's test-coverage map was updated for the rer 0.2.94 reader, and the edition source lock was regenerated. Orbit still runs on rer 0.2.93.

It updates 0.4.2 in place with no migration and keeps every row.

name: Orbit 0.4.2
body: Orbit 0.4.2 is a security release. The agent door now refuses a still-valid access token whose email claim no longer matches the subject's current native email, with a typed 401 or 403 instead of serving the request (conformance point BASE-AGENT-004.sponsor.changed-email). It also carries the record changes made since 0.4.1: each deal's page opens on its next action, with one Activity list and its details beside the work; opportunities, contacts and companies each have their own address, and every record has its own page; record values and workspace settings save as you change them; and each sent message states what Orbit knows about its delivery. Orbit now runs on rer 0.2.93. It updates 0.4.1 in place with no migration and keeps every row.

name: Orbit 0.4.1
body:
## 0.4.1 — 2026-10-29

A release record for commit `79a91f92` (tag `v0.4.1`). Changes since v0.4.0: `MAIL_FROM` is declared as a public variable again, so a Managed install can be configured; and the managed build calls RunEditRun delivery's trusted build at `ff70d729`. The attached `rer-release.dsse.json` is the signed release envelope the platform verifies before it installs this version.

name: Orbit 0.4.0
body:
## 0.4.0 — 2026-10-29

A release record for commit `ed701177` (tag `v0.4.0`). Changes since v0.3.0: the version moves to 0.4.0 on top of the 0.3.0 product; this release adds no product screen, no source behaviour change and no dependency change. The record carries the evidence the platform needs to pin Orbit: the exact-SHA Verify run (https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit/actions/runs/40852232372) and the Run site run (https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit/actions/runs/40856161222) both succeeded, and the complete full-history publication scan found no findings.

The attached `rer-release.dsse.json` is the signed release envelope for this tag (verified with the enrolled just-every key).

The 0.3.0 notes in CHANGELOG.md describe what you get; the "Not in this release" list there still applies.

name: Orbit 0.3.0
body:
## 0.3.0 — 2026-10-20

Changes since v0.2.0 (2026-10-18). An independent release gate ran every homepage job on commit `7c2a636` before this record: once locally at desktop and phone widths, started with the README's one line, and once on a hosted Cloudflare installation with real SendGrid mail. On the hosted installation it took a backup, removed the deployment, deployed again and restored every row. Sending budgets, opt-out links and the end of follow-up on stage moves landed after that gate, so their journeys were run again on commit `0b2bb14`, locally at both widths with real SendGrid mail, and a populated 0.2.0 installation was updated in place to that commit with every row kept. Mentions and the move to rer 0.2.72 landed after that, so the mentions journey was run on commit `ee5d210`, locally at both widths, a populated 0.2.0 installation was updated in place to that commit with every row kept, and an archive made by 0.2.0 restored into it with every row unchanged.

### What you get

- **Deal risks.** Each deal lists what puts it at risk, and cites the record behind each finding: no contact recorded as decision-maker (or another role you require on that deal), overdue promises and tasks, a stage past its stale interval, and reported opens with no reply. If you configure an AI provider, a previewed check also looks for conflicting dates and prices in what you recorded; it sends only those lines and fails whole if a citation is not exact. You can dismiss a finding or change a deal's required roles, each with a reason, and you approve any task it proposes. Nothing here changes the deal or sends mail.
- **Form spam protection.** Published forms refuse submissions that fill a hidden field, arrive too fast or come too often from one form or network. You can also turn on Cloudflare Turnstile for a form. Each refusal is counted with its reason, and suspected spam waits in a list under Forms → Read spam and refusals, where a person can release or erase it.
- **Honest reply and open tracking.** Timelines keep provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and real replies apart, with their source and time. An automatic reply (an out-of-office, say), a reply from someone else or an ambiguous one never stops or completes a follow-up. Orbit adds no open or click tracking of its own.
- **Everything travels in an archive.** Export and restore carry every current kind of data: custom fields and relationships, pipelines and stage history, recurring tasks, reviewed form submissions and spam, captured mail and agent handoff decisions. Restored scheduled messages lose their send approval, so nothing goes out until you approve it again.
- **Follow-up ends when the deal moves.** A scheduled follow-up is cancelled in the same step as any stage move, a won or lost close, a genuine reply or booking, an unsubscribe, a permanent bounce or do-not-contact, and says why. Reopening the deal or replaying the event never brings it back. Each deal's Approved outreach shows Follow-up outcomes: messages the provider accepted, reported deliveries, human replies, meetings booked, stage advances and the deal outcome, each counted on its own, with opens and automatic replies listed as not counted.
- **Sending budgets for each person.** Each user has their own one-to-one budget (1,000 messages a rolling day by default), so one person's volume never holds up another's, under a shared rate of 100 messages a minute. Settings → Sending capacity shows what each person has used and lets the owner change both; each change is audited. A message over a limit stays unsent and names the limit, its value and when it may be sent.
- **Opt-out links by message type.** Settings → Opt-out links decides, for one-to-one email, sequence steps and workflow email, whether Orbit adds List-Unsubscribe headers and an unsubscribe link. One-to-one email starts without them on a new installation; an updated installation keeps them on, as 0.2.0 sent them, until you change it. A rep can remove opt-out from one message as relationship or transactional mail, or add it, and the draft is reviewed again. The approval binds that choice, and the message is delivered exactly so. Each change is audited.
- **Mentions.** Type `@` in a note, a logged call or meeting, a task note or a handoff to mention a colleague; autocomplete offers your active operators and the collaborators who accepted their invitation. Each colleague you mention gets one notification that opens the exact entry, editing notifies only people newly mentioned, and deleting the entry withdraws notifications not yet read. A collaborator who cannot see the record cannot be mentioned until you share it with them or remove the mention; a mention never grants access. Notifications → Mentions lists every entry that mentions you. Mentions stay internal: they never reach a customer or an AI request.
- **Connected products.** Settings → Connected products names the products Orbit works beside (booking, meetings, calling, support, signatures, billing, accounting, Slack, Mailchimp and Buoy), the job each one owns, and whether it reaches Orbit. Today signed Calendly and Cal.com bookings do; the rest say plainly that they are not available in Orbit.
- **Setup-owner protection.** Another operator cannot remove the operator who set Orbit up, and the last administrator cannot remove themselves.
- **Update in place.** An installation on 0.2.0 updates without a reset and keeps every operator, record and setting.

### Not in this release

The homepage calls Orbit an alternative to HubSpot, Pipedrive and Salesforce. CONTRACT.md describes that full product, and the code is still behind it: all 79 published clauses are done, but 20 target clauses are missing and 24 are partial (see the Status table). In particular:

- Mail is sent only through SendGrid (or the managed relay), one recipient at a time. There is no sending from your own Gmail or Microsoft 365 mailbox (OUT-013), no CC, BCC or reply-all (OUT-019), no templates (OUT-014) and no opt-in open or click tracking (OUT-016). There are no multi-step sequences yet (SEQUENCE-001 is partial), and bulk enrollment is missing (SEQUENCE-003).
- Every operator sees every record. Roles and private records are partial (TEAM-005). Only deals have owners; contacts, companies and custom records do not (RECORD-016).
- There are no quotes or signatures (QUOTE-001), no weighted forecasts (FORECAST-001), no shared dashboards (REPORT-002), no workflows that write records (AUTO-002) and no file attachments (RECORD-018).
- Forms are fixed contact forms. Mapping fields to company, deal or custom properties and posting directly from your own site are still to come (FORM-001 is partial).
- There is no Salesforce migration (MIGRATE-003). Orbit has no Zoom, Slack, billing, accounting, help-desk, Mailchimp or Buoy integrations (INTEGRATE-002 to INTEGRATE-008), and Connected products lists them as not available. Booking tools reach Orbit through Sources (INTEGRATE-001 is partial). Calling is partial (CALL-001, CALL-002).
- Mentions are partial (RECORD-017): a mentioned collaborator has no notification inbox yet, so they cannot open their mention; there are no team mentions (TEAM-005), and mentions notify in the app only, not by email, push or Slack (NOTIFY-003).
- Sending budgets cover one-to-one mail today. Sequence budgets and pacing per mailbox arrive with sequences and mailbox sending (OUT-018).
- This release makes no capacity promise. The limits in `seed.json` are estimates until a load test runs.
- The release gate did not exercise live Google or Microsoft capture, inbound mail to an Orbit address, delivery outcomes from a SendGrid Event Webhook, the managed mail relay, Cloudflare Turnstile on a form, or the AI conflict check. Each needs the owner's own accounts, keys, domain or Managed hosting.

### Fixed before release

- The release qualification's full-capacity archive check compared the restored installation with the source and found one extra operator, membership and provision. Restore keeps the restoring installation's own operator on purpose, so that whoever restores is never locked out; the check now sets that operator's rows aside and checks them exactly, and every other table must still match the source row for row.
- Verification occasionally failed to start a test Worker ("Emitted Worker exited before readiness"): the test chose a free port and released it, and Wrangler's own listeners could take that port first. Test ports now come from a range the operating system never hands out on its own.
- An archive made by 0.2.0 could not be restored into this release: the opt-out migration (`0047_opt_out_settings.sql`) keeps one-to-one opt-out on for an installation that already has people, and the restore refused to skip that step. Orbit now runs on rer 0.2.72, which applies that step to the restored data, so a 0.2.0 archive restores with every row and one-to-one opt-out kept on.

### Known issues

- On the managed mail relay (Managed hosting), Orbit cannot add opt-out links yet, so it refuses every message that needs one with "This relay cannot carry your opt-out link yet (OUT-013)". Only a reply in a thread the recipient has answered is sent there, labeled as sent without opt-out. A one-to-one message without opt-out (the setting off, or opt-out removed as relationship or transactional mail) is sent as before. Your own SendGrid account carries opt-out normally.
- A restore brings back imported contacts and companies, but not their import history: archives leave out the import tables, so an import made before the backup cannot be undone on the restored installation.
- Scheduling a draft that was written before another message to the same deal was sent is refused with "Revision already approved, changed, or is no longer permitted". The refusal is correct (the deal's recommendation changed), but the message does not say so; write a new draft.
- While a restore holds the workspace, notification polling answers 503 and fills the browser console. It stops when the restore ends.
- The 0.2.0 known issues this gate did not re-check still stand: a resumed hosted restore needs its confirmation ticked again; a generic `marketing_consent` column is offered as a custom field, not as permission to contact; a deal's contributions can add up past the score's cap of 100 without saying so; after a reload the form page hides its next step behind **Edit saved form** or **Reopen latest publication**; with the managed relay an uncertain send stays delivery-unknown; and the in-app delivery page does not mention the `RER_MAIL_RELAY_SECRET` alternative.

### Back up first, then update

1. Back up and keep the archive private, outside the checkout. Locally, stop `rer dev` and run `rer export --output exports/before-0.3.0.rer`. On a hosted installation, sign in and use Records → Import, duplicate review and data export → Export archive → Prepare export; Orbit emails you a "Confirm it's you" link first, then Download completed archive. `wrangler d1 export` cannot read Orbit's search tables (MIGRATION-RECOVERY.md).
2. Check out v0.3.0, then run `rer install` and `rer setup`. Orbit 0.3.0 pins `@runeditrun/rer` 0.2.72. Locally, setup applies the three pending migrations and keeps your owner, operators, settings and every row; if you changed the owner email under Settings, set `OWNER_EMAIL` in `.dev.vars` to that address first, as setup asks. For a hosted installation, run `rer deploy --env-file .dev.vars.deploy` (with your `--environment NAME`, if you gave one), which applies the same migrations there. Never reset to update.
3. No new setting is needed. `ORBIT_FORM_TURNSTILE_SECRET` is optional, only for a form you opt in to Cloudflare Turnstile. Check Settings → Sending capacity and Settings → Opt-out links once: default limits rise to 100 messages a minute shared and 1,000 a user per rolling day, and one-to-one opt-out stays on until you change it.
4. Check your records, custom fields, drafts and scheduled messages before you resume work.

### Migrations

- `0045_form_abuse.sql`: adds two tables for refused form submissions, one for refusal details and one for the suspected-spam values a person can release or erase. No existing table changes.
- `0046_sending_capacity.sql`: adds an empty table for the owner's changes to the shared sending rate and each user's one-to-one budget; without a row the defaults apply. No existing table changes.
- `0047_opt_out_settings.sql`: adds the opt-out setting for each message type, each draft's opt-out choice and the opt-out state each approval binds. An installation that already has users keeps one-to-one opt-out on; messages approved before the update keep their original unsubscribe group. No existing table changes.
